extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology record; claims are bounded to direct assays and source-stated interpretation.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PmxB4, ent-PmxB4, PMBN, and ent-PMBN interact with LPS in ITC experiments, with PmxB4 showing more productive LPS engagement than ent-PmxB4; simple KD values were not determined for PmxB4/ent-PmxB4 because the curves did not fit a simple model.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Quantitative ITC fitting is bounded to the values and ND notes recoverable from Table S5; no unreported KD is inferred.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NPN uptake assays support outer-membrane disruption by PmxB4 and PMBN, with ent-PmxB4 showing moderate disruption and ent-PMBN weaker or context-dependent disruption across the tested E. coli strains.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PmxB4, ent-PmxB4, PMBN, ent-PMBN in E. coli strains
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-level RFU values were not converted into new numeric rows because the local text/caption supports qualitative source adjudication but not exact point extraction.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Checkerboard/FICI data show stereochemistry-dependent rifampicin potentiation: ent-PmxB4 and PMBN potentiate rifampicin in polymyxin-sensitive E. coli, while PmxB4 and ent-PmxB4 show moderate synergy in mcr-1-positive E. coli.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PmxB4, ent-PmxB4, PMBN, ent-PMBN with rifampicin
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is functional synergy evidence and is not promoted to a standalone direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper interprets the reduced antibacterial activity and altered LPS/OM behavior of enantiomeric species as evidence that stereochemically defined target recognition is required for full polymyxin antibacterial action.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: full-length polymyxin B4 and enantiomeric/nonapeptide analogues
mechanism_claims.limitations: Kept as source interpretation supported by MIC, NPN, ITC, and FICI assays; no extra molecular target is inferred beyond LPS/outer-membrane engagement stated locally.
